title: Introduce RAG Journey Lab: interactive dev shell, step-based playbooks, and plugin playground
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Add a new interactive RAG Journey Lab quickstart with an opinionated developer shell, step-based playbooks, sample plugins, and a guided walkthrough. Useful for onboarding teams that want to prototype tool-calling and incremental retrieval flows locally.
body:
Motivation: Teams repeatedly ask for an opinionated, low-friction developer experience to prototype retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) flows that combine stepwise planning, tool-calling, and live debugging. This PR introduces the 'RAG Journey Lab' — a quickstart that bundles: (1) an interactive dev shell (REPL) for step-by-step intent/plan execution, (2) a set of step-based playbooks that illustrate common patterns (fact lookup, multi-tool workflows, re-ranking, and extract-then-synthesize), and (3) a plugin playground with simple adapter templates for web retrieval, SQL, and a mock external tool.

What this PR contains: - Quickstart scaffold under quickstarts/journey-lab with README, sample indexer, and sample datasets. - Interactive dev shell implemented in TypeScript (devshell/) that supports: start->step->inspect->retry cycle, builtin request/response tracing, and live toggles for batching/kv-cache. - Three curated playbooks (json/yaml) that show incremental prompts and expected assertions for local evals. - Plugin playground with three sample adapters: web-fetch, sqlite-backed knowledge base, and a 'mock-action' tool to demonstrate tool-calling and fallbacks. - Walkthrough docs and screenshots added to docs/quickstarts to show common troubleshooting steps and telemetry hooks. - CI updates: lightweight e2e smoke test (headless) and docs build integration.

Checklist: - [x] Quickstart scaffold and readme - [x] Interactive shell + CLI flags - [x] Example plugins + adapters - [x] Playbooks and assertions for regressions - [x] Unit & smoke tests - [x] Docs walkthrough and screenshots - [x] Telemetry hooks for console-level traces

Compatibility notes: The quickstart targets the hosted Redwood API compatible runtime but includes notes for local private deployments (env vars: REDWOOD_API_URL, REDWOOD_API_KEY). The interactive shell is deliberately minimal and meant for developer iteration; it is not a production runtime. Playbooks are JSON/YAML and structured for easy inclusion in Optimize/eval runs.

How to try locally (short): 1) git clone && cd quickstarts/journey-lab 2) npm i && npm run devshell -- --api-url=${REDWOOD_API_URL} --api-key=${REDWOOD_API_KEY} 3) open ./playbooks/basic-faq.json and run playbook: run-playbook --file playbooks/basic-faq.json 4) toggle plugin: devshell> plugin enable web-fetch

Testing and CI: There was an initial flaky integration test on CI related to request routing; CI logs are summarized below. After addressing the retry backoff and increasing the test timeout the smoke test became stable. Unit tests cover the plugin adapter interface and playbook parser; smoke test exercises the devshell start-run-stop lifecycle.

Commits summary: - Initial scaffold: add journey-lab layout, README, and example dataset - Add interactive dev shell (TypeScript) and REPL command - Add plugin playground and three sample adapters (web-fetch, sqlite, mock-action) - Add step-based playbooks and assertions - Docs: walkthrough, screenshots, and troubleshooting - CI: add smoke e2e and docs build integration - Fix: adjust retry/backoff and test timeouts for flakiness

High-level file changes (small examples shown inline in changed_files): - quickstarts/journey-lab/README.md (new) - quickstarts/journey-lab/playbooks/basic-faq.json (new) - quickstarts/journey-lab/devshell/index.ts (new) - quickstarts/journey-lab/plugins/web-fetch-adapter.ts (new) - quickstarts/journey-lab/plugins/sqlite-kb-adapter.ts (new) - docs/quickstarts/journey-lab.md (new) - .github/workflows/quickstart-smoke.yml (modified) - package.json (modified to add devshell script)

CI summary: - linters: pass - unit tests: pass - integration smoke: failed (test_routing::should_fallback) on first run due to 50ms timeout; rerun succeeded after timeout bump - docs build: pass - total: 4/4 checks passing at merge

Rollout/merge plan: Merge to main, then propagate a short announcement to #quickstarts channel with a short 'getting started' snippet and a link to the docs page. Add entry in quickstarts index and schedule a short demo in the biweekly Dev Experience show-and-tell.

Notes for reviewers: I focused on keeping the devshell code small and self-contained. Feedback welcome on the playbook grammar (currently supports optional assertions and expected-response snippets) and whether to add a Python devshell in the same PR or in a follow-up. The sqlite adapter uses a tiny in-memory DB for examples; for production we recommend the hosted indexer or a dedicated vector DB.
